transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 49 min | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Rita (Verdant Head of Compliance), Marco (Verdant CTO), Leah (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Customer needs deterministic evidence of where data lives and what logs contain, wants ability to lock regionally, use customer-managed keys, and limit token-level logging for PII. Redwood AE/SE outlined options and promised artifacts.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, this is Priya our systems architect. How's everyone doing?
00:12 Rita: Hi Alex, good thanks, we've got a short agenda — worried about data provenance, linkage between logs and raw payloads for audits, and how that maps to GDPR/US finance rules.
00:25 Marco: And from infra side we need to understand keys, evidence for regulators and also what can be redacted before it lands in logs.
00:38 Priya: Great, super helpful. Quick intro to Redwood hosting options — hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, and a private deployment with VPC and on-prem packaged option. We usually recommend Dedicated for teams needing stronger isolation plus predictable throughput; Private if you need full control over networking and KMS.
01:02 Rita: When you say "private" do we get the control plane in our VPC or is it still reaching back to Redwood? We need an audit trail where the control plane doesn't exfiltrate metadata.
01:18 Priya: Private gives you a customer-managed control plane variant, so control-plane traffic can be constrained to your VPC and we can support locked-down peering. There are options for an air-gapped package, but that'll change the update cadence.
01:34 Marco: Ok, so then the question is log provenance. If a regulator asks for a chain of custody for a particular inference, what exactly do we have? Are request/response payloads logged, and can we show which model version served it?
01:47 Alex: Short answer: yes, we can map inference to model version, node id, timestamp, and region. But there are configurable retention and redaction policies. Many finance customers disable full-text request logging and rely on hashed IDs + short-lived traces.
02:10 Leah: We're particularly worried about linkage — e.g., if logs contain a trace id that could be correlated with PII in other systems. Can Redwood strip or tokenize identifiers before they hit your central logs?
02:24 Priya: We support pre-logging hooks and prefix/KV-cache redaction so you can strip PII client-side or in an ingress layer. For Dedicated and Private we can also enable local-only audit logs that never leave the customer's tenancy.
02:42 Rita: For GDPR we need the ability to find all records associated with a subject and also to show deletion proof — immutable audit entries that show deletion action. How do you support legal hold and erasure?
02:55 Priya: We have a couple patterns: logical erasure at the application layer with an event proving deletion, and region-locking so any backups or ledgers are in-situ. For Private deployments, key destruction is in your control if you manage KMS; you can revoke keys which effectively prevents access to encrypted token caches. We provide exportable audit artifacts, but exact proof-of-erasure processes usually need to be baked with the legal team.
03:24 Marco: Are those artifacts machine-readable? Our compliance automation expects JSON manifests for each action.
03:31 Alex: Yes, we can produce structured audit logs — timestamped JSON events with model id, version, route, and optional hashed request id. In hosted mode we retain until your retention policy; in Dedicated you can set longer retention and in Private you control retention entirely.
03:51 Rita: How about encryption at rest and key residency? We have a rule: keys must be in EU for EU data and must be under our KMS.
04:02 Priya: We integrate with customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer customer-managed KMS for specific enterprise contracts but standard hosted is Redwood-managed keys. We'll note that in the diagram.
04:16 Leah: On logging, what about telemetry — things like token-level latency metrics, memory traces, KV cache hits — is any of that considered PII? We need to be careful with correlation.
04:29 Priya: Telemetry is mostly aggregated, but raw traces can include hashed ids. You can flip knobs to only collect aggregates. For private/dedicated you can route telemetry to your SIEM and avoid sending raw traces to Redwood.
04:45 Rita: Another ask: during a regulatory inspection we may need to present a reproducible transcript of a particular inference with model config and quantization profile. Can Redwood capture the exact runtime config per inference?
04:58 Priya: We capture model version, flavor, quantization profile when available, runtime kernels used, and node metadata. For very strict audits we can run an evidence export that bundles model metadata + logs. There can be limits for hosted multi-tenant models — we may expose the model artifact metadata but not the underlying weights.
05:18 Marco: Cost talk — Dedicated vs Private gonna be a big delta. What's typical for a 100 qps production workload?
05:27 Alex: Very rough: Dedicated reserved capacity is often middle of the road — predictable monthly commit. Private will have upfront infra + ops cost. We can share a cost model tailored to your QPS and latency SLOs.
05:38 Rita: Important for procurement is that the vendor can provide evidence of SOC2, ISO27001, and a penetration test report.
05:46 Alex: We'll attach our SOC2 + ISO artifacts and a recent pen test summary. For Private we can agree to a customer-controlled penetration window.
05:58 Leah: On redaction, do you support regex-based scrubbing at the API gateway or do we need to pre-process upstream?
06:06 Priya: There's a flexible plugin model — we can run a scrubbing filter at the gateway or you can pre-process upstream. For Dedicated/Private we can deploy the filter in your network path so Redwood never sees raw PII.
06:20 Marco: About data residency — can we pin a model to a specific region so inference never routes out? For disaster recovery we need a secondary region but that has to be documented for regulators.
06:31 Priya: Yes, routing policies can pin by region and we can configure fallback to a pre-approved secondary region with an approval policy. We keep routing events in the audit logs.
06:42 Rita: One more, chain of custody across teams — if an output is used downstream in analytics, we need to show the chain from input to model to output to storage. Does Redwood provide a lineage ID that persists across pipelines?
06:55 Alex: We provide request IDs and can optionally provide lineage IDs that you can propagate downstream. Many customers take that ID and write it into their data warehouse for traceability. We'll show an example in the architecture doc.
07:10 Marco: Good. Can you also outline what you do for retention of logs in the case of a legal hold versus normal retention? Does legal hold force indefinite retention?
07:22 Priya: We can implement a legal-hold flag that prevents automatic deletion for those IDs — in Dedicated/Private it's fully under your governance. In Hosted it's subject to contractual addendum.
07:34 Rita: We're also evaluating competitors. One is ManagedCloudAI who promised total region lockdown for a premium. How is Redwood different?
07:45 Alex: Redwood's differentiation is the unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private plus transparent performance profiles and built-in evaluation hooks. We try to provide the operational controls customers need without forcing a full self-hosted build.
07:58 Leah: From platform side I need to know how quickly we can rotate keys without downtime, and what's the KV-cache behavior on key rotation.
08:10 Priya: Typical flow: rotate keys in KMS, and we support cache re-encryption or cache invalidation depending on your config. There is a short window for e2e rotation; for very tight SLAs we recommend a staged key roll with pre-warm nodes. We'll document the step-by-step.
08:28 Marco: Ok, this is all high level. Can we get a technical deep dive where you show the logs, the audit artifacts and do a sample deletion flow with keys?
08:39 Alex: Absolutely. We'll set that up. Priya, action for a deep dive and demo of evidence export?
08:46 Priya: Yes, we'll demo evidence export, the pre-logging hook, and a private deployment sketch.
08:52 Rita: Great. A couple more quick Qs — are there limits on log retention for hosted customers due to multi-tenancy?
09:00 Alex: Hosted standard has limits to balance cost; enterprise hosted can have extended retention on a contract. But for absolute control Dedicated/Private are recommended.
09:11 Marco: Do you have references that have gone through financial regulator audits?
09:16 Alex: Yes, we'll anonymize and share a reference summary — can't give names on call but we'll provide case studies.
09:24 Rita: For the evidence export, do we get a signed digest or any tamper-evidence?
09:30 Priya: We can provide signed manifests with checksums. For private installs you can use your own HSM to sign artifacts.
09:40 Leah: Any constraints on on-prem GPUs for private? We run 4x A100 currently.
09:46 Priya: We support a range, but we'll validate kernel/quant path. Some older drivers need small patches; we'll run a compatibility checklist in the deep dive.
09:58 Alex: Ok, let's recap next steps. Priya to send architecture diagram showing hosting options and evidence exports, Alex will send SOC2/ISO and procurement matrix, Verdant to produce compliance flow and sample telemetry extract, and then schedule the deep technical demo for week of Oct 11.
10:18 Rita: Sounds good, thanks.
10:22 Marco: Thanks everyone.
10:25 Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription glitches — names sometimes truncated (e.g., "Priya" as "Pri"), and a few words mis-transcribed ("KV cache" -> "K V cake") in raw transcript.

End of transcript.
